newsitem.title: CHILE: Banco Santiago repays subordinated debt.
newsitem.headline: Banco Santiago repays subordinated debt.

text.p: Chile's largest private bank Banco Santiago said Monday it has extinguished its $1.7 billion subordinated debt owed to the Central Bank.
The debt was cancelled after the expiry of the option period for existing shareholders to buy series E shares which had been issued as part of the deal agreed last year to repay the debt.
The series A, B and C shareholders bought 9.5 million series E shares, the proceeds of which will be paid to the Central Bank, said the statement.
The remaining 35 billion series E shares will remain in the Central Bank's hands, although they will have no voting rights until they are sold.
With the extinction of the debt, all Santiago's A, B, C, D and E stock become common shares with equal rights to dividends.
The bank was one of the last to agree terms with the Central Bank to repay the debt which was incurred when the Bank bailed out private banks during a financial crisis in the early 1980s.
The government had pressed banks to agree to settle their debts as a condition of allowing them to move into new areas of business.
